new_statements.translation: Wɛ is a tone language in which tones have a very high distinctive value, on a par with consonants and vowels. Wɛ has 4 simple tones corresponding to 4 different pitch registers: High (H), Mid-high (h), Mid-low (b), Low (B). A syllable can thus carry a simple tone or a combination of 2 tones. ... Guéré has a system of 6 tonemes that can appear on monosyllables: the 4 simple (level) tones H, h, b, B and the 2 rising tones bh, bH.
new_statements.citation: Bôle-Richard, Rémy. 2006. Unité et diversité du wɛ de Côte d'Ivoire. Journal of West African Languages 33(2): 109-142.
new_statements.locator: §4 'Les tons du wɛ', p. 125, and §4.1 'Le système tonal du guéré', p. 126 (Daho-Doo = survey point G4 in Tableau 1, p. 112)

new_statements.rule_in_words: No stress rule is given anywhere in the source. The Wɛ cluster, of which the author treats Daho-Doo ('Dahoo-Doo', G4) as one Guéré dialect, is described as a tone language with four level tones plus rising and falling contours (13 surface realisations; 6(+2) tonemes in Guéré), whose surface realisation is conditioned by whether the initial consonant is 'high' (voiceless/lenis) or 'low' (fortis voiced). The word 'accent' occurs only for the tone diacritics; word stress or prominence is never mentioned.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. The author notes that some early tone transcriptions (b/h, bH/bh) may be erroneous and were not re-checked in the field (p. 113).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical level: ~600 comparative lexical series (mono- and disyllabic items in citation form) collected 1983-1989 from 17 informants across 8 Wɛ varieties; the Daho-Doo data come from a single informant and appear only as one column in comparative tables. The tone statements are made for the Wɛ cluster and for the Guéré dialect group as a whole, not for Daho-Doo separately.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statements are about the Wɛ cluster (Guéré/Wobè/Nidrou of Côte d'Ivoire) and the Guéré dialect group as a whole. Bôle-Richard 2006 treats 'Dahoo-Doo' as one Guéré dialect (survey point G4, between Guiglo and Taï, one informant), consistent with Wikipedia/Ethnologue ('two mutually intelligible Guere dialects'). Glottolog, however, separates Daho-Doo (daho1238, das) from Wè Southern/Guéré (weso1238, gxx) and groups it with Konobo-Eastern Krahn (east2414, kqo) under 'Konoboic' (kono1271). No source describes Daho-Doo on its own; the catalog entry would rest on the Wɛ-cluster statement plus Daho-Doo's inclusion in that study's data. The 'Doo' of Duitsman, Bertkau & Laesch 1975 is a Klao (klao1243) dialect and must not be confused with Daho-Doo.

sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (the word 'accents' occurs only for tone diacritics). Section 4 'Les tons du wɛ' (p. 125): Wɛ is a tone language with 4 level tones (H, h, b, B) plus rising/falling contours, 13 surface realisations, tone realisation conditioned by the initial consonant; 4.1 (p. 126): Guéré has 6 tonemes on monosyllables. 'Dahoo-Doo' is survey point G4 (Guéré group, between Guiglo and Taï, 1 informant, Tableau 1 p. 112) and appears as a column of forms in comparative tables 13 and 15.

Nothing on stress. Daho-Doo = 'two mutually intelligible Guere dialects', 4,000 speakers (Ethnologue 1996 figure); Kru languages said to have 'some of the most complex tone systems in Africa'; bibliography lists Marchese 1983 Atlas, Marchese 1989 'Kru', Marchese Zogbo 2012.
